skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is owned by other batches; what this reading supports is proposed as commit candidates and in the intake note.
An aggregation or real-world cohort supplies no new therapeutic lever for the reference genotype class; forging hypotheses from it would manufacture a lead.
No compound is newly proposed; cannabidiol is an approved antiseizure medicine and nothing here is sent to BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; every change is proposed as a commit candidate.

group_assessment.weighting: A narrative review with a bibliometric (VOSviewer) step from one paediatric department; WWOX is a top-ten gene with an 18-patient pooled movement row whose primaries are not named. Not a per-author sweep.

entries.proposition: OMIM is the stated source for hypokinesia genes, WWOX among them.
entries.snippet: A review of the OMIM database revealed that mutations in several genes are associated with hypokinesia, include ATP1A3, PIGP, SCN2A, SCN8A, TBC1D24, and WWOX
entries.anchor: Different types of movement disorders, Hypokinesia

entries.proposition: Table 1 hypokinesia set lists WWOX among ten genes.
entries.snippet: ATP1A3, CACNA1A, SCN2A, SCN8A, STXBP1, TBC1D24, WWOX, PIGP, KCNC2, KCNQ2

entries.proposition: Table 2 includes only articles giving types with proportions.
entries.snippet: Only articles that provided specific descriptions of movement disorder types and their corresponding proportions were included in the statistical table (Table 2).

entries.proposition: Dystonia is the main WWOX movement disorder at 83.3%.
entries.snippet: Dystonia is associated with all ten genes, being the main type of movement disorder in GNAO1 (approximately 64.4%), KCNQ2 (62.5%), and WWOX (83.3%) mutations.

entries.proposition: WWOX row (n = 18): stereotypies 0, dystonia 15/18, chorea 0, ataxia 2/18, myoclonus 1/18, tremor 1/18, hypokinesia 5/18.
The text attributes 82.8% myoclonus to CACNA1A, which the CACNA1A row of Table 2 does not show.
entries.snippet: Myoclonus is the main type of movement disorder associated with CACNA1A (approximately 82.8%)
